title: New Housing Fund Rules: Take What You Can, But Don't Treat It as Savings
dek: The housing fund is not savings you can withdraw at will — fraudulent withdrawal gets you pursued for repayment and barred from any withdrawal for three years. But the new rules put renting first in the withdrawal order and scrap the rent-to-income ratio cap, so money you should take, you should still take.
why: Three people in different situations — a self-employed worker, a young professional, a property owner — each run their own numbers, turning the 20 clause changes in the new rules into concrete decisions. The second half, on flexible-employment contributions and the contrast with the public sector, is especially informative.
who: Employees who have a housing fund but aren't sure whether to withdraw or leave it; people considering buying a home, converting a commercial loan to a housing fund loan, or contributing as flexible-employment workers; job seekers trying to judge whether a company is well-run.
skip: The opening chat about how the episode came about and where the three hosts stand can be fast-forwarded; start at 13:10 with Zhou Yi's account of actually using it.

points.h: Six months after auto-withdrawal, I paused it myself
points.body: After Zhou Yi set up Beijing's no-threshold monthly rental withdrawal of 2000 yuan, she found the money slid into another card the moment it arrived, completely decoupled from the mental account for paying rent; when her spending card ran dry at month's end, the money was auto-deducted, which only added friction to daily life. Once she confirmed the housing fund balance earns 1.5% interest, higher than the roughly 0.95% on a one-year bank time deposit, she paused the withdrawal the next day. Yubai points out this contrasts with the advice three years ago to ‘take everything you can, use everything you can’ — two young colleagues in the department have made the same choice. Lao Qian cautions that this is indeed a low-efficiency use of funds, but most people can't achieve the efficiency they imagine for themselves; people just keep fake books for themselves.

points.h: The housing fund is not savings — not being able to take it out is the norm
points.body: Yubai walks through an extreme case: a young person loses their job and goes home with no liquid funds, tens of thousands of yuan sitting in the housing fund, but the home is owner-occupied, so it qualifies neither as buying nor as renting; even if the new rules allow withdrawal under the heading of renovation or property fees, if the family has no such needs, there's nothing to be done. If you take the risk and invent a pretext for fraudulent withdrawal, you'll be pursued to return the entire amount and barred from withdrawing any housing fund for three years. So both approaches hold — ‘take everything you can’ and ‘treat it as forced savings at a rate above demand deposits’ — and the key is the individual's situation.

points.h: The new rules put renting first in the withdrawal order
points.body: This revision adjusts 20 clauses in total. First, renovating an owner-occupied home and paying property fees on an owner-occupied home are included as withdrawal purposes for the first time; the housing fund no longer serves only loan-based home purchases. Second, rental withdrawal used to require that rent exceed a set proportion of household wage income; this version removes that restriction, and renting is placed first in the withdrawal order. Third, flexible-employment workers are formally brought into the system for the first time: self-employed individuals and part-time workers may contribute voluntarily and apply for housing fund loans. In addition, the management center should reply to withdrawal applications within three days and to loan applications within ten days, and nationwide mutual recognition of contribution records is being pushed forward.

points.h: The share of housing fund money lent out has fallen from 70% to 30%
points.body: The figure Lao Qian saw: this year, the share of housing fund contributions lent out is as low as just over 30%, against more than 70% at the peak — a steady decline in just a few years. In other words, the theoretically most stable, lowest-rate, highest-quality lending channel is actually used by only a bit over 30% of people. That directly reflects how low the willingness to buy is. Lao Qian also notes the new rules point toward housing consumption rather than leverage: renting moved to first place, property fees and renovation are withdrawable, thresholds dropped sharply — supporting measures as the real estate market shifts from an incremental to a stock phase, and also echoing the aging trend: the monthly uptick in withdrawal share began in 2023, exactly matching the retirement of the 1960s cohort.

points.h: If you want to buy, be careful about withdrawing your housing fund
points.body: Yubai warns: housing fund loan limits are tied to account balance — in some cities you can borrow 16 times the balance, in others 20 times, varying by city. Guangzhou has several caps; at application, the smallest of the applicable standards governs — for a first or second owner-occupied home the minimum down payment is 20%, so on a 1 million yuan home the loan cannot exceed 800,000; and a monthly repayment exceeding 50% of monthly income also fails. So before withdrawing your housing fund as living expenses, check your city's loan rules. Yubai is also cautious about the buy-side logic that ‘the rental yield is close to the housing fund rate, you're only short a down payment’: you still have to weigh depreciation, price swings, and how to withstand risk once a 600,000 down payment is locked up.

points.h: Flexible-employment contributors carry the full amount alone
points.body: For flexible-employment workers the contribution base and rate are calculated the same way as for employees, but no employer pays half, so one person bears the full 10% to 24%. The base must be self-declared: below 10,000 no proof is needed; above 10,000 you must log into the individual income tax app and pull your tax details as documentation, to prevent inflating the base to extract a higher loan limit. Zhou Yi ran the numbers: 10,000 at 10% to 24% is 1,000 to 2,400 yuan, and this money is not counted toward individual income tax, but it's a loss if you never use it. In addition, most pilot cities require 6 to 12 consecutive months of contributions before you can apply for a housing fund loan, and most do not allow one-time back-payment.

points.h: In the public sector, the housing fund is invisible welfare
points.body: Zhou Yi asked a friend back home with a public-institution post, who readily showed a screenshot of her housing fund account: the monthly deposit is more than twice Zhou Yi's, and the balance already exceeds her savings; the friend lives at home with no rental need, so the housing fund just accumulates as forced savings or future loan capacity, plus she has an occupational annuity, and the contribution base counts bonuses and subsidies in full. Lao Qian adds: the housing fund is tax-free, and on top of that individual pension contributions are capped at 12,000 yuan a year and taxed at 3% on withdrawal — so the public sector already has an extra layer of tax advantage. On the data: in 2025 the national average annual wage for urban non-private unit employees was 129,441 yuan, versus 71,590 yuan for private units — while working hours run the other way.

points.h: Full housing fund contributions are a slice for judging a company
points.body: Lao Qian's judgment on whether ‘a company that pays the housing fund is a more desirable choice’ has not changed at all: a company that pays the housing fund in full respects its employees and respects the rules, which means it is probably well-run across the board, rather than finding workarounds for every policy. He goes further: this points to not making profit maximization the first goal, to treating people as people, and the invisible returns show up elsewhere. Zhou Yi has run the numbers: on a wage base of 100, you actually take home just over 70, but the boss pays out over 130 — everyone along the chain feels aggrieved. Lao Qian cites Ford's Model T wage increase — letting workers afford a car and have time to use it wasn't capitalist conscience, it was simply a better utility function.

quotes.text: It arrived, but because your phone gets so many app notifications you don't look carefully — say it reminds you 2,000 yuan came in, and then it just sits in that card until the end of the month, when my spending card is used up and it gets auto-deducted from that card.
But the fact is people keep fake books for themselves, people withdraw on impulse for all sorts of reasons, people are very good at self-deception.
You really can't treat the housing fund as a deposit, because your bank deposit you can take out at any time, but the housing fund you can't.
And it's the highest-quality lending channel, the rate is so low, yet only a bit over 30% of people actually took a loan — and at the peak, what was that share? Over 70% — in just a few years.
I think a company that pays the housing fund in full shows it respects its employees and respects the rules.

Treating people as people doesn't mean adding cost — it also means one person's spending, the household sector's spending, becomes the corporate sector's income, and the corporate sector's spending becomes the household sector's wages; the two form a virtuous cycle.
Take everything you can, use everything you can — buying a home, building, renovating, repaying a loan, renting, retirement, leaving the country — all of it can be used.
